message.content: Nicolaus Copernicus proposed his heliocentric model during a period of significant tension within Europe. The late fifteenth century saw the rise of humanism, which encouraged new ways of thinking about the universe and humanity's place in it. However, this intellectual awakening coexisted with deep religious conservatism that demanded strict adherence to established doctrine. His work, though revolutionary, remained cactiform in its initial reception, growing slowly despite early support from some scholars. The political landscape was also shifting, with the Catholic Church consolidating power and becoming more suspicious of unorthodox ideas.
